cards.title: Model Joy for Your Kids Despite Tough Childhood
cards.body: Focus on the feeling of enjoyment, not just activities, to show your children a joyful life. Making room for enjoyment means making room for your authentic self.

cards.title: Stop Being a Music Snob With Your Kids
cards.body: Children can teach parents to appreciate music beyond personal taste preferences. Your kids know a good tune when they hear one, even if it differs from your generation's definition.

cards.title: Dads Should Share Diaper Duty Equally
cards.body: Leaving all childcare tasks to your partner is outdated thinking. Equal parenting responsibility strengthens families and models healthy partnership for children.

cards.title: Reading Boosts Your Child's Emotional Intelligence
cards.body: Reading to children improves early literacy skills and emotional intelligence development. It's one of the most impactful parenting investments you can make.

cards.title: Snowplow Parenting Blocks Your Child's Development
cards.body: Removing all obstacles for your child disrupts their development of crucial life skills. Children need the right balance of support and independence to thrive.

cards.title: Calm Yourself to Model Resilience for Anxious Kids
cards.body: If you and your child are both anxious, managing your own worry comes first. Children learn that stress is manageable by watching how parents handle it.

cards.title: Three Postpartum Self-Care Essentials for New Mothers
cards.body: Time outside, regular exercise, and socializing are key to preventing postpartum depression. These three practices form the foundation of postpartum recovery and wellbeing.

cards.title: Ultra-Processed Foods May Rewire Children's Brains
cards.body: New research links childhood diets high in ultra-processed foods to changes in reward circuitry. This raises concerns about dopamine, food addiction, and long-term developmental effects.
